subject: Security & compliance controls — audit logs, customer key options, SSO (triage)

Subject: Atlas security checklist + BYOK/SSO questions

Markus / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Atlas liked the latency profile but procurement needs a short summary of security/compliance options before we can move to legal. They attached our standard security questionnaire (attached) and asked for a brief runbook of how Redwood supports the controls below. Can you confirm the current support surface and any known gaps?

Top asks (high level):
- Audit logs: retention windows available (per-tenant vs global), export formats, access controls for customer ops.
- Customer-managed keys (we call it BYOK): do you support HSM-backed keys? Which KMS providers? Is there a key rotation process we can reference?
- Data retention / deletion: options for short-term retention, selectable retention per workspace, and proof of deletion.
- SSO / SCIM: IdP compatibility and SCIM provisioning scope.

Procurement wants a one-page summary + any artifacts (SOC2 excerpts, sample logs, or KMS diagram). Can you put together a quick position we can share by Monday (2026-08-16)?

Markus / team — triage notes below. I’ve sketched a proposed Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and attached a working spreadsheet (mutual-action-plan-draft.xlsx) with owners and target dates.

Quick answers (summary):
- Audit logs: current product supports tenant-level audit logs with 90-day retention configurable by org-level setting. Exports available in JSON/NDJSON and CSV via the Console and API. Access is RBAC-controlled; auditors can be provisioned read-only via a separate role. Gap: We do not yet support immutable archival (WORM) or automated long-term export to customer S3.
- Customer-managed keys (BYOK): We support KMS integrations with AWS KMS and GCP KMS for model encryption at rest; HSM-backed Cloud KMS providers are supported through those providers. Gap: we do not currently support customer-managed key rotation via API (rotation is UI-only and requires coordinated ops). Also, we don't yet offer on-prem HSM import for a customer's own HSM appliance.
- Data retention / deletion: We have workspace-level retention buckets (90/365/730/indefinite) and a deletion API with audit trail. Proof-of-deletion: we can provide deletion event records but not a signed certificate by default. Gap: automated “verifiable deletion” for legal hold workflows needs engineering work.
- SSO / SCIM: Support for SAML2 IdPs and SCIM provisioning (full user lifecycle). Gap: SCIM custom mappings (complex attribute transforms) are on backlog.

Open questions for product/security owner (Vivek):
1) For Atlas, do they require WORM archival or just a longer retention exported to their own S3?
2) Is HSM import (on-prem appliance) a hard blocker for contract signature?
3) Is a signed deletion certificate required or will a deletion audit log suffice?

Proposed immediate deliverables:
- One-page summary for procurement (Laura) — draft by EOD Thu, 2026-08-13.
- Evidence packet: SOC2 excerpt + sample audit export (Vivek) — by Fri 2026-08-14.
- MAP (attached) owner: Markus — agree on dates and circulate to Atlas.

Attachments: mutual-action-plan-draft.xlsx

Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 14:22:07 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas security checklist + BYOK/SSO questions

Laura — quick technical breakdown and realistic ETA.

Audit logs:
- Current: tenant-level logs, 90-day retention, export via API (NDJSON) and Console. We can provide sample exports today (redact PII).
- Work needed: long-term archival to customer S3 + WORM-style immutability (INF-4219). Estimated 3 sprints (6 weeks) scoped as: export jobs -> signed-presigned-URL ingestion -> retention enforcement + immutability flag.

BYOK / KMS:
- Current: integrate with customer AWS KMS/GCP KMS using standard key policies; we use envelope encryption. HSM-backed KMS supported insofar as the cloud KMS provider supports it.
- Work needed: API-driven key rotation (current flow is UI/ops only) — small engineering task (2 sprints) to expose rotation endpoints and audit events.
- Work needed: on-prem HSM import (full server appliance import) — large scope; will need architecture review and likely be a roadmap-ticket for Q4.

Data retention / deletion:
- Current: deletion API + audit trail. We can produce deletion event logs as proof.
- Work needed: signed-certificate proof (legal) — requires a process + signature service; estimate 2–3 sprints to implement a signed proof-of-deletion artifact.

SSO / SCIM:
- Current: SAML2 + standard SCIM. Custom attribute mapping: on backlog (1 sprint to add key mapping UI + transformations).

Dependencies / blockers:
- Need clarity from Atlas on the required level of immutability vs simple long retention export.
- Legal/Compliance input if signed deletion certificate is required (scope and retention of private keys used to sign).
- Engineering bandwidth: prioritization against other roadmap items; I can commit to API-driven key rotation in next two sprints if we push it to the infra sprint.

I’ll attach a sample audit export (redacted) and SOC2 excerpt to the draft we share.

—
Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Infrastructure & Security

Subject: Re: Atlas security checklist + BYOK/SSO questions — MAP and next steps

Thanks everyone — summarizing the agreed position for Atlas and next steps so procurement/legal have a single doc to review.

Position summary for Atlas (one-page will be attached):
- Audit logs: Tenant-level logs available now, 90-day default retention, exports in NDJSON/CSV. Long-term archival to customer S3 and WORM-style immutability not currently available; roadmap item INF-4219 (estimated 6 weeks after prioritization).
- BYOK/KMS: We support AWS KMS and GCP KMS (including cloud provider HSM-backed keys). API-driven key rotation and audit endpoints are not yet public but will be delivered in ~4 weeks if prioritized. On-prem HSM import is a larger effort and scoped to Q4 roadmap.
- Data deletion: Deletion API + audit trail available; signed deletion certificate is not currently offered out-of-the-box. We can provide deletion event exports as evidence. Implementing a signed certificate is scoped at ~4–6 weeks.
- SSO/SCIM: SAML2 + SCIM provisioning supported; custom attribute mapping on backlog (small work).

Mutual Action Plan (high level):
- 2026-08-14: deliver evidence packet (SOC2 excerpt + redacted audit sample) — delivered.
- 2026-08-16: deliver customer-facing one-page summary (Laura) — in progress.
- 2026-09-30: target delivery for API-driven key rotation (dependent on prioritization).
- 2026-Q4: on-prem HSM import scoping (engineering + security review).

Attachments included for Atlas: Atlas_Security_Questionnaire_v3.pdf, mutual-action-plan-draft.xlsx, atlas-procurement-reqs.xlsx

Sonia — can you confirm which of the three items below is a contract blocker vs nice-to-have? That will help prioritize the work: 
A) WORM-style immutability / signed-archival
B) On-prem HSM import
C) Signed deletion certificate

If A or C are blockers, we’ll propose a temporary carve-out (contractual SLA + delivery timeline) and offer a credit/extension clause until the feature is delivered.

Next: Laura will share the one-page summary and MAP with Atlas by EOD Mon 2026-08-16. I’ll own the MAP communication and follow up with product/security on sprint prioritization.

—
